title: Rocks Pirates
gamePlan: Attack to turn a spare hand card into a chance at drawing two. A high Rocks Pirates density makes the reveal more dependable.
strengths: Leader draw can replenish your hand.
A focused tribe rewards a coherent card package.
weaknesses: A missed reveal costs a hand card.
Off-tribe tech choices reduce reveal consistency.
suggestions: Compare Rocks Pirates density with a recent sourced list.
Review off-tribe slots before adding more situational tech.

title: Green Mihawk
gamePlan: Sequence Characters first, then use the Leader to reactivate DON!! for later actions. The ability locks further Character plays for that turn.
strengths: Reactivating DON!! extends your available resources.
Leader gains power against Slash Leaders.
weaknesses: Using the ability too early prevents further Character deployment.
This leader is announced banned from October 12, 2026.
suggestions: Plan an alternative leader before the October 12 restriction.
Check your turn sequence before activating the Leader.

title: Red Ace
gamePlan: Build around high-power Luffy and Whitebeard Pirates bodies, then use the Leader to grant Rush and apply immediate pressure.
strengths: Qualifying big bodies can attack the turn they arrive.
The Leader gives an explicit tribe and power target for deck building.
weaknesses: The Rush effect requires a qualifying 8000-power body.
Too many expensive bodies can leave an awkward early hand.
suggestions: Count qualifying Luffy and Whitebeard Pirates cards.
Balance high-power threats with early plays and defensive counters.

title: Elbaph Luffy
gamePlan: Use Characters with cost 12 or more to unlock the Leader-granted Blocker effect. Check how your list gets those bodies onto the field.
strengths: Expensive Characters also become defensive bodies.
One leader effect can protect a board of qualifying threats.
weaknesses: The Leader gives no Blocker bonus to smaller Characters.
A hand full of expensive cards needs a realistic early-game plan.
suggestions: Review your early curve before adding more top-end cards.
Compare ways to deploy qualifying Characters in a sourced list.

title: Purple Yellow Pudding
gamePlan: Turn two Life cards face-up while attacking to add a rested DON!! card. Plan how ramp and face-up Life interact with the rest of the list.
strengths: Two colors give access to a broader card pool.
weaknesses: The ramp action requires two Life cards to turn face-up.
Extra DON!! enters rested, so it does not immediately pay normal costs.
suggestions: Check your early defensive options before leaning into expensive threats.
Compare ramp timing and Life support with a recent event list.

title: Purple Enel
gamePlan: Build for a six-card DON!! deck and use the Leader from your second turn to accelerate and allocate resources to a Character.
strengths: Leader rapidly develops and allocates DON!!.
A repeatable resource plan gives your deck a clear engine.
weaknesses: You must build around six DON!! rather than ten.
The main ability does not start until your second turn.
suggestions: Keep the DON!! deck at exactly six cards.
Check that planned normal plays fit the six-DON ceiling.

title: Luffy & Ace
gamePlan: Use named Ace and Luffy cards to benefit from the opponent-turn power bonus, while accounting for the Leader power reduction when a large body is present.
strengths: Named Ace and Luffy cards gain defensive power.
Red and green offer different ways to support your crew.
weaknesses: A 7000-power Character reduces the Leader power.
Unrelated named Characters miss the defensive bonus.
suggestions: Count the Ace and Luffy cards that receive the bonus.
Plan defensive counters for turns when your Leader power is reduced.

title: Nico Robin
gamePlan: Attack with Banish and use Trigger cards from hand to ramp. Balance that resource gain against the cards you give up.
strengths: Leader damage avoids Life Triggers through Banish.
weaknesses: Ramping consumes a Trigger card from hand.
The extra DON!! is rested rather than immediately active.
suggestions: Track the supply of Trigger cards in your list.
Balance late-game threats with defensive options that preserve your hand.
